scope: Post-freeze public-release review findings for Manager 4.17.12

defects.title: Pre-dispatch compatibility-shadow reconciliation blocks target-driven recovery before action dispatch
defects.preconditions: Multi-Hub registry is active; the selected old active Hub is structurally resolvable; its per-instance and compatibility CURRENT checkpoints are missing, corrupt or otherwise unusable; another healthy registered target exists; the invocation requests a target-driven recovery action such as SwitchInstanceId or BindInstancePath.
defects.bad_behavior: Early registry resolution can mark registry mode active without proving compatibility CURRENT health. Top-level startup then unconditionally invokes compatibility-shadow reconciliation before action dispatch for every non-Doctor action. Reconciliation fails on the broken old active CURRENT, so SwitchInstanceId/BindInstancePath/ListInstances and Manager-global actions can be blocked before reaching their own contracts even though recovery/global semantics are intended not to depend on the old active CURRENT.
defects.root_cause: The system proved recovery at function/UI boundaries but did not execute the complete process-entry -> early resolution -> compatibility handling -> action gating -> dispatch path for degraded active-CURRENT states. The engineering state model also lacked an explicit active-Hub-valid / active-CURRENT-invalid state, so diff/risk selection could not require this scenario. This repeats the reachability failure pattern already documented by MGR-DEF-0023, MGR-DEF-0024 and MGR-DEF-0026.
